subject: Post-demo: deployment routing options, legacy GPU exit and next steps
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Maya Rao <maya.rao@kitehealth.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 02 Sep 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: deployment routing options, legacy GPU exit and next steps

Hi Maya / Samir —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps based on our conversation: 

1) Summary of needs we heard
- Production traffic: ~5M tokens/day initially, expected to grow 2–3x in 12 months.
- Hard requirement: EU data residency (customer PII stays in EU).
- Current footprint: mix of an old on-prem GPU cluster (periodic heavy runs) + existing LLM API (VendorTextAI) for online features.

2) Deployment options that fit (pros/cons at a glance)
- Hosted API (fastest, minimal ops) — good for quick time-to-value; may need egress/region considerations for EU residency.
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) — predictable throughput, easiest route for steady production; we can reserve EU capacity.
- Private (VPC/on-prem) — best for air-gapped or regulated workloads and full control during migration from legacy cluster.

3) Migration considerations we discussed
- Lift-and-shift vs hybrid: we can route realtime requests to Hosted/Dedicated while running batch jobs on your legacy cluster (gradual cutover).
- VendorTextAI migration: tokenization/response-format differences, and rate-limit patterns need validation.

Attachments: TCO-estimate-KiteHealth.xlsx (cost sketch), SOC2-evidence-summary.pdf (attestation highlights).

Proposed next steps:
- Can you confirm the team that will own procurement + compliance? (you mentioned Procurement and Security)
- If you’re interested, we’ll schedule a 60m technical deep-dive with infra (to capture KV cache needs, latency SLOs) and a separate procurement sync.
- If agreeable, we’ll propose a short MAP (mutual action plan) with a 4-week POC scope: model parity checks, EU-hosting validation, and migration pilot.

Could you confirm availability for a tech deep-dive next week (Sep 8–10)? Also flag any blackout dates for cutovers.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
alex@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0134

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Data residency: must be EU for both inference and logs. We operate out of Frankfurt and would prefer an EU-only deployment (no cross-region fallback without explicit approval).
- Legacy cluster: we run periodic batch re-training and heavy scoring on a GPU farm in our colo. That cluster is on a strict change freeze until mid-Oct. We want to avoid disrupting batch jobs during the POC.
- VendorTextAI: yes, we currently route ~60% of requests to them for online features. We’re concerned about semantic drift during model swaps and about rate limiting during ramp.

Procurement: looping in Procurement (procurement@kitehealth.com) — they’ll need a baseline SOW and an outline of security controls.

MAP: happy to see a 4-week pilot but we need the pilot to be non-invasive to our nightly batch and must validate EU-hosting + encryption-in-transit/rest.

Available for a tech deep-dive Sep 9 (morning CET) — does that work for your infra folks?

Cheers,
Maya Rao
Director, Product Engineering | KiteHealth
maya.rao@kitehealth.com

Note: we may also include Samir (platform lead) on the tech call — Samir, can you confirm availability?

Maya / Samir / Procurement —

Great — Sep 9 morning CET works for our infra. Agenda I propose for the tech deep-dive (60m):
- 10m: introductions + goals for pilot (non-invasive to batch, EU residency)
- 20m: infra mapping (networking, KV cache, existing auth + KMS)
- 20m: migration anchors (tokenization alignment, latency SLOs, fallback behaviors)
- 10m: MAP / next steps + deliverables (SOW, POC success criteria)

Three MAJOR scoping options we’ll present on the call (we’ll bring cost sketches):
A) Rapid Hosted + EU controls: use Hosted API with strict EU-region routing, short POC; lowest ops but requires legal sign-off on EU-only processing.
B) Dedicated EU pool: reserved capacity in Frankfurt, predictable latency, easier KV/caching control for parity with your online features.
C) Private VPC: full customer-managed VPC in your tenancy (or on-prem install) — highest compliance control, longer lead time and procurement.

For migration from VendorTextAI and the legacy cluster we recommend a phased MAP:
- Week 0–1: model parity checks (prompt sets, response diffing), tokenization tests, perf baseline.
- Week 2: pilot routing 5–10% online traffic to Redwood Dedicated (canary) while batch stays on legacy cluster.
- Week 3–4: expand pilot if parity and SLAs met; handoff SOW to procurement.

Related links: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1gX-demo-MAP-KiteHealth (POC draft) | HubSpot: HS-9876543

Please reply with the procurement contact name and an SSO/KMS owner so our security team can prep the compliance packet.

Thanks,
Alex
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Hi all —

A couple quick technical guardrails from infra/ops perspective before the tech call: 

- Tokenization parity: we will run a side-by-side tokenization + response-diff pipeline during Week 0–1. This will identify any prompt engineering work required to match VendorTextAI outputs.
- KV cache behavior: Dedicated pools support shared KV cache and deterministic latency; Hosted can do caching but we’ll need to validate hit-rates for your traffic patterns.
- Legacy cluster migration: propose a staged approach that keeps nightly batch jobs untouched. We can publish a migration-playbook (attached) that maps steps for cutover, rollback, and incident playbooks.

Attachment stub: migration-playbook.md (outline of steps, rollback criteria, required stakeholders).

I’ll bring concrete test scripts and a checklist to the tech call; happy to own the Week 0–1 runbook if you want Redwood to lead that effort.

-Rishi
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
